title.narrative: Reduction of HIV transmission and HIV-related morbidity, mortality, disability and social and economic impact in Myanmar - Myanmar (01-Jan-2013-31-Dec-2016)

description.narrative: Myanmar has the second highest number of HIV-positive people in Southeast Asia. The program supported by this grant aims to reduce transmission and treatment HIV related morbidity, mortality, disability and social and economic impact. The program target group are sex workers and men who have sex with men (MSM), injecting drugs users (IDU) and people living with HIV. The program is consistent with the National Strategic Plan (NSP) on HIV and AIDS and its Operational Plan and is prioritized according to epidemiological data and the HIV disease burden. The proposal of this grant is to increase the number of people living with HIV receiving support, with people receiving the package of care and treatment and to strengthen and expand the technical and implementation capacity of national staff as well as the organizational capacity of civil society and community-based organizations. The current grant plans to provide harm reduction services including treatment maintenance and needle and syringe exchange. It targets IDUs and helps strengthen the health and community systems and program management and administration.
